gloss: be finished, come to an end; finish, make an end of; vessel; kidneys
summary: The verb is to come to the end of something: a work finished (Gen 2:1–2; Exo 39:32), a store spent (Gen 21:15), eyes and soul spent with longing (Psa 84:3; 119:81–82), people consumed (Psa 90:7); in the piel, to finish a thing or to make an end of people (Exo 32:10). The noun כָּלָה is that end in full, the “full end” Yahweh makes of the nations but not of Jacob (Jer 30:11), the end decreed (Isa 10:23; Dan 9:27); תַּכְלִית is an end or limit, כִּלָּיוֹן a failing or annihilation. Two common nouns stand beside these whose tie to “finish” is not shown: כְּלִי, any made thing — vessel, implement, weapon, instrument, jewel — and כִּלְיָה, the kidneys, with the heart the hidden self that Yahweh tries (Jer 17:10). Ugaritic and Phoenician-Punic kly (finish, annihilate) and Aramaic כְּלֵי (be finished) share the verb’s sense; the kidney word has its own cognates across Semitic.

words.gloss: vessel, implement; weapon; instrument; article, jewel
words.summary: Any made thing that holds, serves or is carried: a pot or jar, the tabernacle’s utensils, a warrior’s weapons, a musician’s instrument, a bride’s jewels, a traveller’s baggage. How it comes from the root of “finish” is not shown: no cognate checked here shares the meaning (the Targums use מָאנָא), so its tie to the root rests on its spelling alone. The New Testament takes up its figures through σκεῦος: the potter’s vessel (Rev 2:27 from Psa 2:9) and vessels made for honour or dishonour.

senses.definition: A container of clay, wood, metal or skin, which holds water, oil, grain or the like and can be emptied, broken or made unclean.

evidence.note: “Any כְּלִי of clay into which one of them falls, whatever is in it shall be unclean, and you shall break it.”
“Any כְּלִי of wood or garment or skin or sack, any כְּלִי with which work is done.”
The widow is to pour the oil “into all these כֵּלִים”, and set aside the full.
“There is no more כְּלִי”, and the oil stopped.
“The כְּלִי he was making of clay was spoiled in the potter’s hand, and he made it again another כְּלִי.”
“You shall dash them in pieces כִּכְלִי יוֹצֵר, like a potter’s vessel”; taken up in Rev 2:27.
Moab has settled on his lees and “has not been emptied מִכְּלִי אֶל־כֶּלִי, from vessel to vessel”.
Ruth may drink from the כֵּלִים the young men draw.
“Every open כְּלִי with no cover bound on it is unclean.”
“I am forgotten like a dead man out of mind; I have become כִּכְלִי אֹבֵד, like a broken vessel.”
Coniah, “a כְּלִי no one delights in”, cast out: a vessel as a figure for a man God has set aside. Also Hos 8:8; Jer 48:38.
“Lips of knowledge are a precious כְּלִי.”

senses.definition: The furniture and utensils of the tabernacle and temple, made to the pattern shown, anointed, carried by the Levites, taken to Babylon and brought back.

evidence.note: “The pattern of the tabernacle and the pattern of all its כֵּלִים.”
“All the כְּלֵי of the tabernacle in all its service.”
Anoint the tabernacle “and all its כֵּלִים, and it shall be holy”.
The Levites over the tabernacle and all its כֵּלִים; they shall carry it.
The sons of Kohath carry “all the כְּלֵי of the sanctuary” once Aaron has finished (כַּלֹּת) covering them.
The holy כְּלֵי brought up into Solomon’s house.
“Depart, go out from there … be clean, you who bear the כְּלֵי of Yahweh.”
Part of the כְּלֵי of the house of God carried to Shinar.
Cyrus brings out the כְּלֵי of the house of Yahweh.
Your brothers brought as an offering “as the sons of Israel bring an offering בִּכְלִי טָהוֹר, in a clean vessel, to the house of Yahweh”.

senses.definition: A warrior’s or hunter’s equipment: his weapons and armour, carried for him by his armour-bearer; by extension the instruments with which God or man brings death.

evidence.note: “Take your כֵּלִים, your quiver and your bow, and go out to the field and hunt.”
Jonathan says to “the young man who bore his כֵּלִים”, his armour-bearer.
Saul to his armour-bearer: “draw your sword and thrust me through.”
David put Goliath’s כֵּלִים in his tent.
“Neither my sword nor my כֵּלִים have I brought.”
Simeon and Levi: “כְּלֵי חָמָס, weapons of violence, are their swords.”
“No כְּלִי formed against you shall prosper.” Isa 54:16: the smith who brings forth a כְּלִי for his work.
“I will turn back the כְּלֵי מִלְחָמָה, weapons of war, that are in your hands.”
He has prepared for him “כְּלֵי מָוֶת, instruments of death”; his arrows.
“Yahweh and the כְּלֵי of his indignation, to destroy the whole land.” Also Jer 50:25.
Six men, each with his כְּלִי מַפָּצוֹ, his shattering weapon.
“How the mighty are fallen, and the כְּלֵי מִלְחָמָה perished!”

senses.definition: An instrument for music, and any tool or implement for work: the instruments of song in the temple service, a farmer’s yoke and gear.

evidence.note: The Levites appointed as singers “בִּכְלֵי שִׁיר, with instruments of song: harps, lyres and cymbals”.
Trumpets, cymbals and כְּלֵי הַשִּׁיר when the glory filled the house.
“With the כְּלֵי שִׁיר of David the man of God.”
They invent for themselves כְּלֵי שִׁיר like David.
“I will praise you בִכְלִי נֶבֶל, with the harp.”
“The threshing sledges and the כְּלֵי of the oxen for wood”: their yokes and gear.
Elisha boiled the oxen’s flesh בִּכְלֵי הַבָּקָר, with the oxen’s gear.
No hammer or axe “or any כְּלִי of iron” heard in the house while it was being built.
Ambassadors sent by sea “בִּכְלֵי גֹמֶא, in vessels of papyrus”: boats.

senses.definition: A thing made and owned: jewels of gold and silver, a person’s goods and gear, the baggage of a camp or of an exile; of dress, a thing proper to a man.

evidence.note: The servant brought out “כְּלֵי כֶסֶף and כְּלֵי זָהָב, and garments” for Rebekah.
Each woman shall ask her neighbour for “כְּלֵי כֶסֶף and כְּלֵי זָהָב, and clothing”. Also Exo 11:2; 12:35.
“As a bride adorns herself with her כֵלִים”: her jewels.
“You took כְּלֵי תִפְאַרְתֵּךְ, your fine jewels of my gold and my silver.”
Brooches, earrings, rings, every כְּלִי of gold.
Jacob to Laban: “You have felt through all my כֵּלִים; what have you found of all the כְּלֵי of your house?”
Saul “is hidden among the כֵּלִים”: the baggage.
David left his כֵּלִים with the keeper of the כֵּלִים.
“As is the share of him who goes down to battle, so shall be the share of him who stays by the כֵּלִים.”
“Prepare for yourself כְּלֵי גוֹלָה, baggage for exile.” Also Jer 46:19.
“A man’s כְּלִי shall not be on a woman, nor shall a man put on a woman’s garment.”
“Do not regard your כְּלִי, for the good of all the land of Egypt is yours.”

phrases.gloss: his armour-bearer (he who carries his gear)

evidence.locator: Psa.2.9, כְּלִי → σκεῦος; σκεῦος renders כְּלִי ×211

evidence.note: “He shall rule them with a rod of iron, as the σκεύη of a potter are broken”: Psa 2:9’s כְּלִי יוֹצֵר.
“Has not the potter authority over the clay, to make from the same lump one σκεῦος for honour and another for dishonour?”: the potter of Jer 18:4–6.
σκεύη of wrath, and (Rom 9:23) σκεύη of mercy.
One who cleanses himself “will be a σκεῦος for honour, sanctified, useful to the master”.
Saul “is a chosen σκεῦος of mine, to bear my name before the Gentiles”.
Moses sprinkled the tabernacle “and all the σκεύη of the ministry” with blood: the כְּלֵי of Exo 40:9.

evidence.locator: Jer.18.4, כְּלִי → ἀγγεῖον (twice); ἀγγεῖον renders כְּלִי ×13

evidence.note: The wise took oil ἐν τοῖς ἀγγείοις, in their vessels.

words.gloss: be finished, come to an end, be spent, fail; finish, complete, make an end of, consume
words.summary: Qal: of something reaching its end — a span of time or a work completed, a store used up, eyes, soul or flesh spent with longing or grief, people consumed; and of evil “determined”, settled to its end. Piel: to finish doing a thing (the usual “when he had finished speaking”), to complete a work or a span of days, to carry wrath or a word through to its end, and to make an end of people: consume, destroy. Pual, twice: be finished.

stems.gloss: be finished, come to an end; be spent; fail, pine; be consumed; be determined

senses.gloss: be finished, be completed; be fulfilled
senses.definition: Of a span of time, a season’s work or a building reaching its end and so being complete; of a word reaching its fulfilment.

evidence.note: “Thus all the work of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting was finished (וַתֵּכֶל), and the sons of Israel did according to all that Yahweh commanded Moses.”
“The seven years of plenty that were in the land of Egypt came to an end.”
In the eighth month the house was finished in all its parts: seven years in building.
Ruth gleaned with Boaz’s young women “until the end of (כְּלוֹת) the barley harvest and the wheat harvest”: the harvest season from Passover to Weeks.
“The harvest is past, the summer is ended (כָּלָה), and we are not saved.”
Like gleanings when the vintage is done.
He will not forsake you “until all the work for the service of the house of Yahweh is finished”.
The singing and trumpets continued “until the burnt offering was finished”.
From the day of the foundation of the house of Yahweh “until it was finished”.
“That the word of Yahweh by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled (לִכְלוֹת)”: a word brought to its end in the event. Also 2Ch 36:22.
“When the shattering of the power of the holy people is finished, all these things shall be finished.”
He shall prosper “until the indignation is finished, for what is decreed shall be done”.

senses.gloss: be spent, used up, run out
senses.definition: Of a store or supply coming to its end: water, flour, grass.

evidence.note: “When the water in the skin was spent, she cast the child under one of the bushes.”
“The jar of flour shall not be spent (לֹא תִכְלָה), and the jug of oil shall not fail (לֹא תֶחְסָר).”
“The grass is withered, the herbage is spent, there is no green thing.”
“The vintage will fail, the gathering will not come.”

senses.gloss: fail, be spent with longing; pine, waste away
senses.definition: Of eyes, soul, heart or flesh spent with waiting, longing or grief, or wasting away: life’s strength used up toward what it looks for.

evidence.note: “My soul longs, indeed it is spent (כָּלְתָה), for the courts of Yahweh.”
“My soul is spent for your salvation; I hope in your word.”
“My eyes are spent (כָּלוּ) for your word, saying, When will you comfort me?”
My eyes fail for your salvation.
“My eyes fail while I wait for my God.”
Our eyes failed, looking for help in vain.
“My eyes are spent with tears.”
The wild asses’ “eyes fail because there is no herbage”.
“The eyes of the wicked shall fail.” Also Job 17:5.
“My spirit is spent (כָּלְתָה); do not hide your face from me.”
“My flesh and my heart fail (כָּלָה), but God is the rock of my heart and my portion for ever.”
“My kidneys are spent (כָּלוּ כִלְיֹתַי) within me”: Job’s longing to see God for himself.
“Do not forsake me when my strength fails.”
“When your flesh and your body are consumed.” Also Job 33:21.
“My life is spent with grief, and my years with sighing.”

senses.gloss: come to an end, vanish; be consumed, perish
senses.definition: Of people, their days or a power coming to an end: consumed by sword and famine, vanishing like smoke or a cloud; of wrath or oppression, ceasing.

evidence.note: “The wicked shall perish (יֹאבֵדוּ) … they vanish (כָּלוּ), in smoke they vanish.”
“As a cloud is consumed (כָּלָה) and goes away, so he who goes down to the grave does not come up.”
“My days are consumed (כָלוּ) like smoke.”
“We are consumed (כָלִינוּ) by your anger, and by your wrath we are dismayed.”
“I am consumed by the blow of your hand.”
“Those who forsake Yahweh shall be consumed (יִכְלוּ).”
“They shall be consumed by the sword and by famine.”
The men of Judah in Egypt “shall be consumed (וְתַמּוּ) by the sword and by famine until they come to an end (כְּלוֹתָם)”: תָּמַם beside it.
A third “shall be consumed by famine in your midst”.
The plastered wall falls “and you shall be consumed in its midst”.
“By the breath of God they perish, and by the blast of his anger they are consumed.”
“My days … come to their end without hope.”
“That my days should be consumed in shame.”
“I am Yahweh, I do not change; therefore you, sons of Jacob, are not consumed (לֹא כְלִיתֶם).”
“The kindnesses of Yahweh, that we are not consumed (לֹא תָמְנוּ), for his compassions do not come to an end (לֹא כָלוּ).”
“In a very little while the indignation will come to an end.”
“The extortioner is at an end (אָפֵס), destruction has ceased (כָּלָה), the oppressor is consumed (תַּמּוּ) from the land.”
“The ruthless is brought to nothing, the scoffer is consumed (כָלָה).”
“All the glory of Kedar will come to an end.”
Egypt’s helper and helped “will all perish together”.
“The rod of his fury shall fail.”

senses.definition: Of harm intended against someone: carried to its end in the mind, settled and fixed.

evidence.note: “If he is angry, know that evil is determined (כָלְתָה הָרָעָה) by him.” Also 1Sa 20:9.
“Evil is determined against our master and all his house.”
Haman saw “that evil was determined (כָלְתָה) against him by the king”.

stems.gloss: finish, complete; spend; accomplish; make an end of, consume, destroy

senses.definition: To bring an action or a work to its end: to finish speaking, eating, building; to complete what was begun.

evidence.note: “And by the seventh day God had finished (וַיְכַל) his work which he had made, and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made.” Quoted Heb 4:4.
“So Moses finished the work.”
“When she had finished giving him drink, she said, I will draw for your camels also, until they have finished drinking.”
Yahweh went his way when he had finished speaking with Abraham.
“When Jacob finished commanding his sons, he drew his feet into the bed and expired.”
When Moses had finished writing the words of this law in a book.
“Moses finished speaking all these words to all Israel.”
The ark’s window: “to a cubit you shall finish it from above.”
When Solomon had finished building the house of Yahweh.
Hiram finished all the work he did for King Solomon.
When Solomon had finished praying all this prayer.
When Jeremiah had finished speaking all the words of Yahweh.
“When they had finished eating the grain they had brought from Egypt.”
“Finish (כַּלּוּ) your works, your daily task.”
“Keep close to my young men until they have finished all my harvest.”
“The man will not rest until he has settled (כִּלָּה) the matter today.”
“I will perform against Eli all that I have spoken … beginning and finishing (הָחֵל וְכַלֵּה).”
Joab began to count, but did not finish.
When they have completed the days of the altar’s cleansing.

senses.gloss: finish off (a field), reap to the end
senses.definition: In the gleaning law, to reap a field to its very edge, leaving nothing standing; Israel is forbidden it, so the corner remains for the poor and the stranger.

evidence.note: Set at the feast of Weeks (Lev 23:15–21): “When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not finish off (לֹא תְכַלֶּה) the corner of your field when you reap, nor gather the gleanings of your harvest; you shall leave them for the poor and for the stranger: I am Yahweh your God.”
“You shall not finish off the corner of your field in reaping”: the same law.
Ruth, a stranger and poor, gleans in Boaz’s field “until they have finished (כִּלּוּ) all my harvest”: the law kept.
“When you have finished tithing all the tithe of your increase in the third year”, to give it to the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless and the widow.

senses.definition: To bring a span of life or a supply of strength to its end: to spend one’s years, to spend strength for nothing, to spend arrows on an enemy.

evidence.note: “All our days pass away in your wrath; we finish (כִּלִּינוּ) our years like a sigh.”
“If they listen and serve, they shall spend (יְכַלּוּ) their days in good and their years in pleasures.” Also Job 21:13.
“So he made their days end (וַיְכַל) in vanity.”
The servant: “I have spent (כִלֵּיתִי) my strength for nothing and vanity; yet surely my judgment is with Yahweh.”
“I will spend (אֲכַלֶּה) my arrows on them.”
When you have completed these days, lie on your right side.

senses.definition: Of Yahweh’s anger, to pour it out to its full measure; of man’s mind, to bring an evil purpose to pass.

evidence.note: “Thus my anger shall be accomplished (וְכָלָה, qal) … they shall know that I Yahweh have spoken in my zeal, when I have accomplished (בְּכַלּוֹתִי) my fury on them.”
“Now I will soon pour out my fury on you, and accomplish (וְכִלֵּיתִי) my anger on you.”
“To accomplish my anger against them in the midst of the land of Egypt.” Also Ezk 20:13, 21.
“Yahweh has accomplished (כִּלָּה) his fury; he has poured out his fierce anger.”
“Compressing his lips he brings evil to pass (כִּלָּה רָעָה).”

senses.gloss: make an end of, consume, destroy
senses.definition: To bring people or a thing to an end: to destroy utterly, wipe out; of eyes, to make them fail.

evidence.note: “Let me alone, that my anger may burn against them and I may consume them (וַאֲכַלֵּם), and I will make of you a great nation.”
Moses: why should Egypt say he brought them out “to consume them from the face of the earth”?
“I will not go up in your midst … lest I consume you on the way.” Also Exo 33:5.
“Separate yourselves from this congregation, that I may consume them in a moment.” Also Num 17:10.
Phinehas turned back my wrath, “so that I did not consume the sons of Israel in my jealousy”.
In the land of their enemies “I will not reject them … to destroy them utterly (לְכַלֹּתָם), to break my covenant with them; for I am Yahweh their God”.
“You may not make an end of them at once, lest the beasts of the field increase on you.”
If you forsake Yahweh, “he will turn and do you harm and consume you”.
“Fight against them until they are consumed.”
“I did not turn back until they were consumed.” Also 2Sa 22:38.
“You shall strike Aram in Aphek until you have made an end of them.” Also 2Ki 13:19.
“I will send the sword after them, until I have consumed them.” Also Jer 49:37.
“They have devoured Jacob, and consumed him.”
“You have consumed them, but they refused to take correction.”
“I have consumed them with the fire of my wrath.”
“Consume them in wrath, consume them, that they be no more.”
“He makes an end of the blameless and the wicked.”
“They had almost made an end of me on earth.”
The curse will lodge in the thief’s house “and consume it, its timber and its stones”.
“Would you not be angry with us until you had consumed us, so that there should be no remnant?”
When the locusts had made an end of eating the grass of the land.
He will consume the glory of his forest.
“Consumption and fever that make the eyes fail (מְכַלּוֹת עֵינַיִם)”: the piel of failing eyes. Also 1Sa 2:33; Job 31:16.
“If I have made the eyes of the widow fail.”

senses.definition: Of a work brought to its end by another: the heavens and earth, a collection of prayers.

evidence.note: “Thus the heavens and the earth were finished (וַיְכֻלּוּ), and all their host.”
“The prayers of David the son of Jesse are ended.”

parallels.note: “Be complete, be consumed”, beside it of people and of Yahweh’s mercies.
“Lack, fail”, beside it of the widow’s flour and oil.
“Long for”, beside it of the soul that is spent with longing.

greek.gloss: bring to an end, complete, accomplish

evidence.locator: Gen.2.2, כָּלָה → συνετέλεσεν; Gen.2.1 συνετελέσθησαν; Lev.23.22 συντελέσετε; συντελέω renders כָּלָה ×26 and more in its inflected forms

evidence.note: Quoting Isa 10:22–23, where כִּלָּיוֹן and כָלָה stand: “For he is finishing (συντελῶν) the word and cutting it short in righteousness, for the Lord will make a short work upon the earth.”
“What will be the sign when all these things are about to be accomplished (συντελεῖσθαι)?”

evidence.locator: Psa.84.3, כָּלָה → ἐκλείπει; Psa.90.9 ἐξελίπομεν; ἐκλείπω renders כָּלָה ×18

evidence.note: “I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail (ἐκλίπῃ).”
“That when it fails, they may receive you into the eternal dwellings.”

words.summary: The end made in full: almost always Yahweh’s, in the phrase עָשָׂה כָלָה “make a full end”, which he will do to the nations among whom Israel is scattered but never to Israel itself (Jer 30:11; 46:28). Paired with נֶחֱרָצָה, it is the end decreed (Isa 10:23; 28:22; Dan 9:27). A few times it stands as an adverb, “altogether”.

senses.definition: An end made of a people with nothing left: destruction carried through to the last.

evidence.note: “I will make a full end (אֶעֱשֶׂה כָלָה) of all the nations where I have scattered you, but of you I will not make a full end; I will correct you in measure.” Also Jer 46:28.
“The whole land shall be a desolation; yet I will not make a full end.”
“Go up through her vine rows and destroy, but do not make a full end.”
“Even in those days, says Yahweh, I will not make a full end of you.”
“In your great mercies you did not make a full end of them nor forsake them, for you are a gracious and merciful God.”
“My eye spared them from destroying them, and I did not make a full end of them in the wilderness.”
Ezekiel: “Ah, Lord Yahweh, will you make a full end of the remnant of Israel?”
“With an overflowing flood he will make a full end of her place.” Also Nam 1:9: “affliction shall not rise up a second time.”
“He will make a full end, a sudden one, of all who dwell in the land.”
Hailstones in fury “for a full end”.
When Rehoboam humbled himself, the anger of Yahweh turned from him, “not to destroy him to a full end”.
He shall stand in the glorious land, “with destruction in his hand”.

senses.definition: The end Yahweh has determined, named with נֶחֱרָצָה “decided”: settled beforehand and certain to come.

evidence.note: “For a full end, and that decreed (כָלָה וְנֶחֱרָצָה), the Lord Yahweh of hosts will make in the midst of all the land”: after “a remnant shall return” (Isa 10:22); quoted Rom 9:27–28.
“Do not scoff … for a full end, and that decreed, I have heard from the Lord Yahweh of hosts upon the whole land.”
“Until the full end, and that decreed (וְעַד־כָּלָה וְנֶחֱרָצָה), is poured out on the desolator”: Isaiah’s phrase at the close of the seventy weeks.
Jonathan knew “that it was determined (כָלָה הִיא) by his father to kill David”.

senses.definition: As an adverb, to the full, entirely.

evidence.note: “I will go down and see whether they have done altogether (כָּלָה) according to the outcry that has come to me.”
“When he lets you go, he will surely drive you out from here altogether.”

parallels.note: “Decided, decreed”, paired with it of the end Yahweh determines.

phrases.gloss: a full end, and that decreed

evidence.note: The disciples ask of the temple’s overthrow, “and of the συντέλεια of the age”; Jesus answers with Daniel’s abomination of desolation (Mat 24:15).
“Now once at the συντέλεια of the ages he has appeared to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.”

words.gloss: kidneys; the inner self, mind and feelings
words.summary: Always plural: the kidneys of a sacrificed animal, burnt with their fat on the altar; and a man’s kidneys as his hidden self, set beside the heart, which Yahweh tests and the risen Christ claims to search (Rev 2:23). Its cognates (Akkadian kalītu, Ugaritic klyt, Aramaic כּוֹלְיָא) all mean kidney; how it belongs to the root of “finish” is not shown, and it may be a word of its own that only shares the letters.

senses.definition: The two kidneys with the fat on them, taken from the animal and burnt on the altar with the fat as Yahweh’s portion.

evidence.note: “And the two kidneys and the fat that is on them, which is by the loins, and the lobe on the liver, which he shall remove with the kidneys.”
“All the fat that covers the entrails … and the two kidneys and the fat on them, and burn them on the altar.”
The same from the sin offering.
The same from the guilt offering.
At the consecration, Moses burns them on the altar.
Yahweh’s sword “fat with the fat of the kidneys of rams”: Edom’s slaughter as a sacrifice.
“With the fat of the kidneys of wheat”: the finest of the wheat.

senses.gloss: kidneys as the inner self: thoughts, feelings, conscience
senses.definition: A person’s kidneys as the seat of what is hidden in him: his desires, feelings and conscience, which instruct, rejoice and are pierced with grief, and which God formed and tests.

evidence.note: “I Yahweh search the heart, I test the kidneys, to give every man according to his ways, according to the fruit of his doings.”
“Yahweh of hosts, who judges righteously, who tests the kidneys and the heart.” Also Jer 20:12.
“The righteous God tests the hearts and kidneys.”
“Examine me, Yahweh, and prove me; try my kidneys and my heart.”
“You are near in their mouth and far from their kidneys”: the inner self set against the lips.
“I will bless Yahweh who has counselled me; also my kidneys instruct me in the night.”
“My kidneys will rejoice when your lips speak right things”, beside “my heart” (Pro 23:15).
“My heart was embittered and I was pierced in my kidneys.”
“For you formed my kidneys; you wove me in my mother’s womb.”
“My kidneys are spent within me”, with longing to see God.
His archers “split my kidneys and do not spare”: Job’s inmost being wounded.
“He has caused the arrows of his quiver to enter my kidneys.”

parallels.note: “Heart”, its constant partner for the inner man.

evidence.locator: Jer.17.10, כִּלְיָה → νεφρούς; νεφρός renders כִּלְיָה ×26

evidence.note: “All the ecclesias shall know that I am he who searches kidneys and hearts, and I will give to each of you according to your works”: the words of Jer 17:10.

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܟܘܠܝܬܐ (kulitā), for νεφρός in Rev 2:23, where the risen Christ takes up Jer 17:10: the same word as Hebrew כִּלְיָה.

senses.definition: As the Hebrew: the hidden thoughts and desires, searched with the heart.

evidence.note: “I am he who searches the kidneys and the hearts.”

words.summary: The point where a thing ends: the far end of a house, the boundary of light and darkness, the utmost reach of searching, and so “complete” hatred. Five uses, all late or in Job and the Psalms.

senses.definition: The end or edge of a thing, and the farthest point that can be reached.

evidence.note: Meremoth repaired “from the door of the house of Eliashib to the end (תַּכְלִית) of the house of Eliashib”.
“He has inscribed a circle on the face of the waters, at the boundary (תַּכְלִית) of light and darkness.”
“Man puts an end (קֵץ) to darkness, and searches out to every limit (תַּכְלִית)”: beside קֵץ.
“Can you find out God by searching? Can you find out the Almighty to the utmost (עַד־תַּכְלִית)?”

senses.definition: Used as an adverb: to the full, with nothing held back.

evidence.note: “I hate them with complete hatred (תַּכְלִית שִׂנְאָה); they have become my enemies”: those who hate Yahweh (Psa 139:21).
An oath is “the end (πέρας) of all dispute” among men.

words.summary: Two uses: the eyes spent with longing in exile (Deu 28:65), and the destruction decreed on Israel’s land, from which a remnant returns (Isa 10:22). Each answers a sense of the verb. The name of Naomi’s son Kilion (Rut 1:2) is spelt the same but filed as a name.

senses.definition: The spending of the eyes with longing and grief.

evidence.note: Among the nations, “Yahweh will give you there a trembling heart, and failing of eyes (כִלְיוֹן עֵינַיִם), and languishing of soul.”

senses.definition: A destruction carried to its end, as decreed.

evidence.note: “Though your people Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant of them shall return; destruction (כִּלָּיוֹן) is decreed, overflowing with righteousness”; quoted Rom 9:27–28.

words.summary: Once: the eyes of parents whose children are given to another people, looking for them and spent with longing.

senses.definition: Of eyes that look for what does not come, until they are spent.

evidence.note: “Your sons and your daughters shall be given to another people, and your eyes shall look and fail (וְכָלוֹת) for them all the day.”

words.summary: Once, in the plural construct: the gold of the temple’s lampstands and tongs was מִכְלוֹת זָהָב, gold brought to completeness, the purest. The sense rests on this one verse and its form.

senses.definition: Gold worked to its full purity: “completeness of gold”.

evidence.note: “The flowers, the lamps and the tongs of gold, that was מִכְלוֹת זָהָב”: of the purest gold (1Ki 7:49 has “gold”, and 2Ch 4:20 “pure gold”).

words.summary: Once: every completed thing has its end, but Yahweh’s commandment has none.

senses.gloss: completeness, a thing brought to its end
senses.definition: Anything brought to completion, which for that reason has a limit.

evidence.note: “To every completeness (לְכָל־תִּכְלָה) I have seen an end (קֵץ); your commandment is exceedingly broad.”
“I am with you always, until the συντέλεια of the age.”

cognates.gloss: (N) be spent, used up; (D) finish off, annihilate

evidence.note: "/k-l-y/: N nkly “to be spent”; D ykly, tkly, tkl “to finish with, annihilate” (cf. H. k-l-y)".
"ykly ṯpṭ nhr 1.2:IV:27 “he finishes off Judge River”—from G /k-l-y/ “to be finished”".
"yn ... d nkly b dbḥ 4.213:24 “wine ... which was used up at the sacrifice”".

cognates.note: Ugaritic has the Hebrew senses in the same stems: the simple and passive of a supply used up (Gen 21:15), the doubled stem of finishing off an enemy (Exo 32:10).

evidence.note: "v. pi'el 1. COMPLETE": CIS i 124 (Pu) nqyb klty, “into the rock was it excavated; I completed it on day x of the month”; "2. ANNIHILATE": KAI 38 (Ph) ršp mkl, “Rasap-the-Annihilator”.

cognates.note: Punic and Phoenician, with the Hebrew piel’s two senses: finishing a work (Exo 40:33) and making an end of people.

evidence.note: "[*taklit: cf. Heb. k-l-y, expend] n.f. EXPENSE, EXPENDITURE": KAI 18 (Ph) btklty, “at my own expense”; KAI 37 A tklt yrḥ ʾtnm, “the expenditures for the month of Etanim”.

cognates.note: The same pattern as Hebrew תַּכְלִית; in Phoenician what is spent, in Hebrew where a thing ends. Both answer the verb’s “spend, use up”.

evidence.note: "to be finished, gone. Ber. 39ᵃ כַּלְיָא ברכה the benediction is finished … B. Mets. 79ᵃ וקא כליא קרנא and the capital itself is used up … Yoma 69ᵇ כ׳ עלמא the world would come to an end".

cognates.note: Babylonian Aramaic. Jastrow files under the same headword a verb “restrain”, which answers Hebrew כלא, not this root.

evidence.note: "extinction. Lam. R., introd. … לא תשוון כ׳ גמירא do not exterminate (them) entirely".

cognates.note: Aramaic, in a phrase like Hebrew עָשָׂה כָלָה “make a full end”.

evidence.note: kidney; testicle (×282).
klyt “kidneys”, set beside the Ethiopic word; the scan’s OCR of the Ethiopic is unreadable.
Among the body-part terms Ugaritic shares with Ethiopic: “heart (lb), liver (kbd), kidneys (klyt)”.
"kidney. Ḥull. 97ᵃ.—Pl. כּוֹלְיָן … Targ. Lev. III, 4; … Targ. Is. XXXIV, 6 כָּלְיַת constr.": the Targum’s word for the כְּלָיוֹת of the offerings.
Syriac kulitā; the Peshitta’s word in Rev 2:23.

doctrine.statement: The heavens and the earth and all their host “were finished”, and by the seventh day God “had finished his work which he had made” and rested from it (Gen 2:1–2). The fourth commandment counts that work: “in six days Yahweh made heaven and earth, the sea and all that is in them, and rested the seventh day” (Exo 20:11). Hebrews quotes Gen 2:2 and draws the conclusion: “the works were finished from the foundation of the world” (Heb 4:3–4). So creation is a finished work, done in six days and complete before the first sabbath; nothing in scripture has it continuing, or being added to by slow change, since.

Yahweh says he will make a full end (כָּלָה) of all the nations where he scatters Israel, “but of you I will not make a full end; I will correct you in measure” (Jer 30:11; 46:28). He gives the reason himself: “I am Yahweh, I do not change; therefore you, sons of Jacob, are not consumed” (Mal 3:6); even in their enemies’ land he will not destroy them utterly, “to break my covenant with them” (Lev 26:44); and Israel’s confession owns that it was his mercy, not their faithfulness (Neh 9:31; Lam 3:22). Isaiah sets the same word on the other side: a destruction decreed, from which only a remnant returns (Isa 10:22–23), and Paul quotes it of the Jews of his day, of whom a remnant was saved (Rom 9:27–28). So the nation is judged but never ended, because its survival rests on Yahweh’s unchanging covenant, while the powers that scatter it come to their end.

The pair כָּלָה וְנֶחֱרָצָה, “a full end, and that decreed”, is Isaiah’s for the judgment Yahweh had settled on the land (Isa 10:23; 28:22). Daniel uses it at the close of the seventy weeks: after Messiah is cut off, a people of a prince to come destroy the city and the sanctuary, and desolation continues “until the full end, and that decreed, is poured out” (Dan 9:26–27). Jesus, asked when the temple would be thrown down, points to “the abomination of desolation spoken of by Daniel the prophet” and says “this generation shall not pass away until all these things take place” (Mat 24:2–3, 15, 34). The decreed end of Dan 9:27 is therefore the Roman destruction of Jerusalem and its temple in AD 70.

With the heart, the kidneys stand for what is hidden in a person: they counsel him at night, rejoice, and are pierced with grief (Psa 16:7; Pro 23:16; Psa 73:21); one can be near God with the mouth and far from him in the kidneys (Jer 12:2). Yahweh formed them (Psa 139:13) and tests them, “to give every man according to his ways” (Jer 17:10; 11:20). The risen Jesus uses Jeremiah’s words of himself: “I am he who searches kidneys and hearts, and I will give to each of you according to your works” (Rev 2:23). He does this as the one to whom the Father “has given all judgment” (Jhn 5:22, 27): God’s own searching of the inner man is carried out through his Son.

note: Drafted for Lev 23:22 (לֹא תְכַלֶּה פְּאַת שָׂדְךָ). BDB keys not claimed: k.bk.af כִּלְיוֹן (Naomi’s son Kilion, Rut 1:2) and k.bk.ad כְּלוּהוּ/כלוהי (Ezr 10:35) are people, left for name entries; a.dc.ad וְאֻכָל (Pro 30:1), which BDB would repoint וָאֵכֶל “and I am spent” from this verb, is left as the text points it, a name; the zero-token cross-reference keys k.bl.aa, k.bm.ae, k.bm.af, m.bx.ac and w.ap.ad were not claimed. The verb tokens BDB files here at Gen 23:6 and 1Sa 6:10 are of כלא (restrain), not this root. כְּלִי and כִּלְיָה stand without any cognate that shares “finish”: no Semitic cognate of כְּלִי was found in the vendored dictionaries (Phoenician and Aramaic use other words for “vessel”), and the kidney word’s cognates (Akkadian, Ugaritic, Aramaic, Syriac; Arabic kulya and Ge’ez kʷəlit were not checked in their own dictionaries) all mean only kidney. Both may be separate roots sharing the letters; kept here as the rule asks. Arabic has no verb kly ‘finish’ (Lane’s كلو is thin, the late volumes); Ge’ez not checked (Dillmann, Leslau). Akkadian kalû ‘hold back’ answers כלא, and kalû/kullatu ‘all’ answer כלל: not cited here. Doctrine ‘decreed-end’ states the AD 70 reading of Dan 9:27 for the user’s review; ‘creation’ states the six-day reading. מִכְלָה’s sense rests on 2Ch 4:21 alone.
